avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction may reduce ranitidine efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative herbal supplements

caution_supplements.name: Iron supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Ranitidine reduces gastric acid, potentially decreasing iron absorption
caution_supplements.action: Separate dosing by 2 hours; monitor for anemia symptoms

caution_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Reduced gastric acid may impair calcium absorption
caution_supplements.action: Take calcium with acidic beverages; monitor calcium levels if chronic use

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin B12 supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Long-term ranitidine use may reduce B12 absorption from food sources
caution_supplements.action: Monitor B12 levels; consider supplementation if deficiency develops

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing foods/beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Caffeine may increase gastric acid production, potentially reducing ranitidine effectiveness
caution_foods.action: Limit coffee, tea, chocolate, and caffeinated beverages during therapy

caution_foods.name: Spicy and fatty foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Can stimulate gastric acid secretion and irritate GI lining
caution_foods.action: Avoid large, spicy, or high-fat meals; eat smaller, frequent meals

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Can increase gastric acid production and irritate mucosa
caution_foods.action: Limit or avoid alcohol consumption during acid-related disorder treatment

monitoring_notes: Monitor for efficacy in acid suppression and symptom relief; assess for vitamin B12 and calcium deficiency with prolonged use. Note: Ranitidine was withdrawn from US market in 2020 due to NDMA contamination concerns.
